94:5.intro: Ease is not promised after the hardship, but with it. Notice: it may already be present somewhere in your life, small and easy to miss.
questions: What is the hardest thing you are carrying right now? Name it plainly, without softening it.
Where, even a little, is there ease alongside it today? A person, a breath, a moment of relief?
If ease is already travelling with this hardship, what changes in how you hold it?
94:5.intention: Today I will notice one small ease and thank Allah for it.

2:286.theme: You are not asked for more than you can bear
2:286.intro: Read this as a gentle correction to the voice that says you cannot cope. The verse does not deny that it is heavy; it says the weight is measured to you.
questions: What feels like too much right now? List it as it comes.
Which of those things is truly yours to carry today, and which belong to tomorrow, or to others, or to Allah?
Think of a past burden you believed you couldn't bear. What got you through it?
2:286.intention: I will carry only today's share, and hand the rest to Allah.

13:28.intro: The verse names a cure for restlessness without dismissing it. Before reading, notice where your body holds tension.
questions: Where do you feel unrest in your body right now? Chest, stomach, shoulders?
What do you usually reach for to quiet your heart, and does it work for long?
What would a few minutes of real remembrance (dhikr, du'a, silent presence) look like for you today?
13:28.intention: I will give my heart a few minutes of remembrance before I reach for anything else.

2:152.intro: Notice the direction of the verse: when you remember Allah, you are remembered. You are held in mind long before you feel it.
questions: When did you last feel remembered, truly seen by someone, or by Allah?
What gets in the way of remembering Him lately? Busyness, guilt, numbness?
If you are already remembered, what might you let go of trying to earn?
2:152.intention: I will remember Allah once today in my own words, and trust that I am remembered.

93:3.intro: This was revealed to comfort a heart that feared abandonment. Let it be said to you, by name, in your own situation.
questions: Where do you feel abandoned or unseen right now, by people or by Allah?
What is the story your mind tells about why?
Imagine Allah saying 'I have not forsaken you' to that exact feeling. What happens inside you?
93:3.intention: When the feeling of abandonment rises, I will answer it with this verse.

39:53.intro: Addressed to 'My servants who have transgressed against themselves', the first words are 'O My servants', not 'O sinners'. Notice the tenderness of how you are called.
questions: What do you most struggle to forgive yourself for?
What would change if you believed Allah's mercy was larger than that thing?
What is one honest step toward Him you could take today? A du'a, a repair, a prayer?
39:53.intention: I will turn to Allah with what I am ashamed of rather than hide it from Him.

3:139.theme: Do not weaken, do not grieve
3:139.intro: It was revealed after a painful loss. It doesn't forbid sorrow; it refuses to let sorrow convince you that you are finished.
questions: What loss or setback are you still carrying?
Where has it made you feel smaller or weaker than you really are?
What strength or part of your faith is still intact, even now?
3:139.intention: I will let myself grieve without letting it define me.

9:40.intro: Said in a cave, with pursuers close, by a man to his frightened companion. Imagine the stillness in that moment.
questions: What is your 'cave' right now, the narrow place where you feel cornered?
Who or what is with you there that you may be overlooking?
How would you act today if you truly believed 'Allah is with us'?
9:40.intention: In my narrow place, I will say: Allah is with us.

65:3.intro: Tawakkul is not passivity; it is doing your part and releasing the outcome. Read it slowly, noticing what you are gripping.
questions: What outcome are you trying hardest to control?
What is your part in it, and what is not yours?
What would it feel like to put your effort in and set the result down?
65:3.intention: I will do my part, then release the outcome to Allah.

2:216.intro: A verse for a plan that fell apart. It doesn't call the pain unreal; it reminds you that your view is partial.
questions: What did you want that you didn't get, or what happened that you didn't want?
What has a past disappointment turned out to give you, in hindsight?
What would it mean to trust that Allah sees the part you can't?
2:216.intention: I will hold my disappointment with trust that I see only part of the picture.

50:16.intro: He knows what your soul whispers to you. Nothing in you is hidden from Him, and that can be frightening, or deeply comforting.
questions: What do you whisper only to yourself, the thing you've never said aloud?
What does it feel like to know He already hears it, with full knowledge and mercy?
What would you say to Him if you didn't have to polish it?
50:16.intention: I will speak honestly to Allah, without polishing my words.

2:186.intro: Notice that there is no intermediary in this verse. The question is asked, and the answer comes straight back: I am near.
questions: What do you most want to ask for, if you let yourself ask?
What stops you from asking? Doubt, shame, feeling unworthy?
What would it mean to treat the answer, 'I am near', as true right now?
2:186.intention: I will ask Allah for what is on my heart tonight, plainly and specifically.

20:25.intro: Musa (peace be upon him) asked for an inner capacity before the task itself. A du'a for when the heaviness is in your chest.
questions: What task or conversation ahead feels bigger than you?
Where is your chest tight? What is it holding?
What would 'expansion' look like, not the problem disappearing, but you having more room within it?
20:25.intention: Before I face the thing I dread, I will make this du'a.

57:23.intro: A verse about loosening our grip: what passed you by was never going to be held by your effort alone.
questions: What have you lost or missed out on that you keep replaying?
What would it mean to grieve it, and still loosen your grip?
What blessing in your hands right now are you at risk of overlooking?
57:23.intention: I will name one thing I still have and be grateful for it.

12:86.intro: Yaqub (peace be upon him) lost a son and wept until his sight faded. He did not hide it; he took it to Allah. This is grief done with faith.
questions: What sorrow have you been holding quietly, or in front of people but not in front of Allah?
What would it mean to complain to Him, as Yaqub did, with full honesty?
Is there someone safe you could also share this with?
12:86.intention: I will bring my sorrow to Allah tonight, in full.

3:173.intro: Said when people warned that the odds were against them. The warning increased them in faith. Notice what fear does to you, and what this phrase does back.
questions: What are you afraid of right now? What are people telling you to fear?
What does 'Allah is sufficient for us' take off your shoulders?
Which fear is realistic and needs action, and which just needs to be handed over?
3:173.intention: When fear speaks loudly, I will answer with: Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakeel.

64:11.intro: Notice the promise here: whoever believes in Allah, He guides their heart. The guidance is for the heart, in the middle of the hardship.
questions: What has recently struck you that you didn't expect or choose?
How is your heart responding right now: resisting, numb, softening?
What would 'guidance for the heart' look like in this? Calm, clarity, patience?
64:11.intention: I will ask Allah to guide my heart through what has happened.

7:23.theme: Owning a mistake and coming back
7:23.intro: The first words of repentance in human history: no excuses, no blaming, just 'we have wronged ourselves'. Adam and Hawwa (peace be upon them) came back instead of hiding.
questions: What are you carrying that you haven't owned or brought to Allah?
What's the difference between guilt that pushes you away and guilt that brings you back?
What would turning back look like today, in words, in action, or in repair?
7:23.intention: I will own what I've done, ask forgiveness, and not stay in hiding.

21:87.intro: Yunus (peace be upon him) called out from the belly of the whale, in layers of darkness. His du'a admits his own part and affirms Allah's perfection.
questions: What does your 'darkness' look like at the moment?
Which part of it is circumstance, and which part, if any, did you contribute to?
What happens if you say 'there is no god but You, glory be to You' from inside that place?
21:87.intention: From wherever I am, I will call on Allah with this du'a.

17:82.intro: The Quran describes itself as healing and mercy for believers. Reading it can be an act of care for yourself, not just duty.
questions: How has your relationship with the Quran felt lately: close, distant, guilty, avoided?
What part of yourself needs healing most right now?
If the Quran were speaking directly to that wound, what do you hope it would say?
17:82.intention: I will read a few verses today slowly, as if they were written for me.
